checks.independent_reasoning: Source line 326 literally says infimum; lines 341-346 use supremum over positive exponents in the body. With H>=1 an admissible exponent remains admissible after decreasing it. Rational convergents give infinitely many degree-one numbers with H(p/q)<=C_xi q, so each fixed 0<w<1 is admissible for every transcendental real xi and each n>=1. Thus the infimum is zero in the body's positive domain, or minus infinity if unrestricted; the reported positive lower bound cannot refer to that infimum.
checks.counterevidence_and_severity: The body already uses the correct extremum, and the preserved publisher HTML also explicitly uses supremum. Only that abstract has been compared, not the whole Version of Record. The one-word local definition error therefore stays Minor; no core theorem failure is implied.
